messages:
alex: Heads up — saw a weird latency spike on prod-rt yesterday, looks like cache misrouting when two tenants get batched.
jonathan: Can you drop the nsys trace? p99 numbers?
alex: Uploaded nsys capture link: https://internal/trace/2038765432 (nsys + nvtx markers included)
alex: Quick summary: p99 went from ~42ms -> 118ms for small-chat workload when batch window=10ms.
maria: I pulled the nsys timeline — NVTX shows frequent kernel toggles between 'attn_fused' and 'matmul_merge'. Kernel handoff cost ~6-8ms each time.
maria: Reuse ratio for prefix keys dropped from 78% -> 31% during spike (KV misses jumped). Looks like requests from tenant B evicting tenant A prefixes.
jonathan: Which kernel selector path triggered the matmul fallback? any threshold logs?
maria: yes — selector logged "fallback_path=GEMM_SPLIT" at 12:34:11. Command used to capture:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --output=trace_2038765432 --sample=none --nvtx
```
maria: also exported perfetto slices and an nvtx-to-perfetto map for the timeline. Noticed an nvtx region just before dispatch where batcher did a tenant-merge op.
perf-bot: perf-report: p50=19.4ms p95=60.2ms p99=118.3ms tokens/sec drop=18% (compared to baseline)
infra-bot: current batching config: window_ms=10, max_batch=64, tenant_isolation=best-effort
alex: quick mitigation tried: reduced window_ms to 4ms and set tenant_isolation=strict on one GPU pool — p99 dropped back to ~50ms but throughput decreased ~6%. This suggests the missstorm is caused by cross-tenant eviction under the old policy.
jonathan: Action items: 1) add per-tenant KV bands + eviction bias, 2) tweak kernel selector to prefer fused attention path for short sequences, 3) add NVTX markers on kernel decision points and batcher merge code. @maria can you open a perf ticket with traces + command lines?
maria: Yep — will open PERF-XXXX with the nsys and perfetto exports, attaching nvtx regions, selector logs, and a small reproducer.
alex: thanks — tagging @eng-runtime to keep an eye. :mag:
